lines: 18 listed coins (TROLL, CARDS, BUTTCOIN, USELESS, TTT, WIF, POPCAT, AI16Z, BONK, FARTCOIN, PNUT, GOAT, HAWK, LIBRA, MELANIA, PONKE, PEPE, TRUMP) left out: older than the free candle feed reaches (about six months), so the launch is not in the data. Pools picked by symbol search (check these are the real coins): TTT = TokenTime Two, HAWK = Hawk Tuah, LIBRA = LIBRA, MELANIA = Melania Meme, PONKE = PONKE, PEPE = Pepe, TRUMP = OFFICIAL TRUMP.
3 giants studied. The typical one took 33 days from launch to its top, went 3.14x from the day-1 close, and on the WAY there fell 30%+ 2 times and 50%+ 2 times (worst dip before the top: 95%).

So a rule that sells everything on a 50% giveback is out of the typical giant before the top: the clips must fund the ride, and the moonbag must trail wider than a giant's dips (95%+), or it never sees the top.

From a $500 entry on the day-1 close, summed over all 3: hold $15,514, giveback $1,806, trail35 $1,441, clipsTrail35 $1,200, clipsTrail50 $1,200, clipsTrail65 $1,200, trail50 $1,185, trail65 $829 (the exact top would have been $27,912). Best rule: hold: never sold (rode it to wherever it is now).

Entry day against the multiple to the top (median): day 0 3.34x, day 1 3.14x, day 2 5.17x, day 3 4.68x, day 5 9.35x, day 7 11.02x, day 14 13.01x; the first 30% pullback after a 2x: 3.14x (3 of 3 gave one).
After the top: 1 of 3 are now 80%+ under it (median 7 days to lose half from the top). Riding it back is the default outcome; the rules above are what stand between a $500k position and zero.

Day-3 fingerprint, giants against 4 duds (coins that pumped and died): on day 3 the giants stood at 0.84x their day-1 close with 0.7x day-1's volume and 33% were still above the day-1 close; the duds at 1.02x, 0.28x the volume, 50% above. Not a clean separation yet: add more duds and giants to src/giants.json.
